original_question: When cone filtrations between Σ_{n+1,2d} and P_{n+1,2d} are built by ordering the monomials of I_{n+1,d}, which structural properties of the chosen monomial order determine whether adjacent cones become equal or remain strictly separated, and how do those order-theoretic properties control the resulting pattern of equalities and inequalities in the filtration?
target_in_paper: The nearest paper-faithful target is the unnumbered research question in §3.3 (Cones along Toric Varieties), immediately after Example 3.2, asking which properties of a monomial order affect the occurrence of cone equalities and strict inequalities in the cone filtrations produced by the paper’s construction.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: cone filtrations between Σ_{n+1,2d} and 𝒫_{n+1,2d} that are obtained from an ordering of I_{n+1,d}, and specifically the problem of explaining when adjacent inclusions C_i ⊆ C_{i+1} collapse to equalities or remain strict. It also stays close to the paper’s actual focus and does not drift into the broader toric-variety generalization of Open Problems 5–6.
missing_details: The paper’s question is meaningful in the non-Hilbert cases; this restriction should be stated explicitly, since in the Hilbert cases Σ_{n+1,2d} = 𝒫_{n+1,2d}.

The ambient spaces should be specified: ℱ_{n+1,l} is the real vector space of homogeneous degree-l forms in n+1 variables, while the projective varieties V_i live in ℙ^k over ℂ and positivity is tested on real points V_i(ℝ).
The set being ordered should be defined exactly: I_{n+1,d} = {α ∈ ℕ_0^{n+1} : |α| = d}.
The indexing parameter should be made explicit: k = k(n,d) = dim(ℱ_{n+1,d}) - 1 = binom(n+d,n) - 1.
The chosen monomial order should be tied to the ordered list α_0, …, α_k (taken in decreasing order) and the resulting monomial basis m_j(X) = X^{α_j}.
The cones C_i must be defined, not just mentioned: first define H_i, then its Zariski closure V_i ⊆ ℙ^k, and finally C_i = C_{V_i}.

The operator data behind C_i should be included: the Gram map 𝒢 : Sym_{k+1}(ℝ) → ℱ_{n+1,2d}, A ↦ f_A, and the associated quadratic form q_A, since C_W is defined by existence of A ∈ 𝒢^{-1}(f) with q_A nonnegative on W(ℝ).
The index range should be explicit: i = 0, …, k - n, so that the filtration is Σ_{n+1,2d} = C_0 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ C_{k-n} = 𝒫_{n+1,2d}.
The phrase adjacent cones should be pinned down to the inclusions C_i ⊆ C_{i+1}.
To stay paper-faithful, the lexicographic benchmark should be recalled: in non-Hilbert cases the lex order gives the strictness pattern in (6), which is what Example 3.2 is contrasting against.
The motivating counterexample from the paper should be mentioned: for a non-lexicographic order on I_{3,5}, Example 3.2 shows Σ_{3,10} = C_4, so the initial part of the filtration collapses.
No nilpotency condition, asymptotic clause, or phrase such as for all sufficiently large m appears in this problem; it is a finite-dimensional exact question.
refined_question: Fix a non-Hilbert pair (n+1,2d). Let ℱ_{n+1,l} be the real vector space of homogeneous degree-l forms in n+1 variables, let I_{n+1,d} = {α ∈ ℕ_0^{n+1} : |α| = d}, and choose a monomial order on I_{n+1,d}, written in decreasing order as α_0, …, α_k with k = binom(n+d,n) - 1; set m_j(X) = X^{α_j}. Using the paper’s Gram-matrix construction, define H_i = { [z] ∈ ℙ^k : there exists x ∈ ℂ^{n+1} with (z_0, …, z_{n+i}) = (m_0(x), …, m_{n+i}(x)) } for i = 0, …, k - n, let V_i be the Zariski closure of H_i in ℙ^k, and let C_i = C_{V_i} = { f ∈ ℱ_{n+1,2d} : there exists A ∈ 𝒢^{-1}(f) such that q_A|_{V_i(ℝ)} ≥ 0 }. Which order-theoretic properties of the chosen monomial order determine, for each i, whether the adjacent inclusion C_i ⊆ C_{i+1} is an equality or is strict, and hence determine the complete pattern of equalities versus strict inclusions in the resulting filtration Σ_{n+1,2d} = C_0 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ C_{k-n} = 𝒫_{n+1,2d}?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting §3.3 rather than the main closure/interior results: Section 1 gives the construction of the filtration from an ordering of I_{n+1,d}, the associated Gram map, and the lexicographic strictness pattern (5) and (6) on pp. 2–3. Example 3.2 in §3.3 then shows that changing the monomial order can alter that pattern: for a particular non-lexicographic order on I_{3,5}, the paper proves Σ_{3,10} = C_4, so part of the filtration collapses, unlike the lexicographic case. Immediately after this example, the paper explicitly asks which properties of a monomial order influence the occurrence of cone equalities and inequalities. Open Problem 5 is nearby but broader, since it passes from monomial-order-induced varieties to arbitrary projective toric varieties, so it is not the nearest target of your draft.
